content: {"rule": "K-G4", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge uses verses (Matthew 1:18, 25 and Luke 1:34) to break challenger link C3, which is exactly the act the rule's final sentence governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D2 vs C3 (Matthew 1:18, 25): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 \"before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost\" and Matthew 1:25 \"knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son\" contradict C3's claim of espousal union; [L2] πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν (prin ē synelthein, Strong's G4250/G4905, before coming together) and οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν (ouk eginōsken, Strong's G1097, was not knowing); [L3] Luke 1:34.", "rule_words": "counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge uses to break a link is counted this way.", "room": "'A verse the judge uses to break a link is counted this way': reading (a) verses used to break a link must meet the same quote-the-pressing-sentence-and-name-the-round condition in order to count, versus reading (b) the rule only governs tallying unanswered witnesses and places no requirement on link-breaking itself; I weighed (a) because on reading (b) the final sentence does no work at all.", "why": "The judge broke the link using Matthew 1:18, 25 and Luke 1:34 but quoted only the scripture text itself, never a sentence of an earlier round that pressed these verses against the link or a premise, and named no round whatsoever, so the verses used to break the link are not counted the way the rule requires."}
